title: Mock 3 · Rules of the Road
blurb: Deadlines, approvals and categories: the compliance calendar every RIA lives by.

questions.q: Apart from the track-record-and-AUM route, how else can a fund qualify to offer the new asset class?
options: By appointing experienced fund managers with a proven track record in managing large portfolios
By obtaining a banking licence from RBI
By listing the AMC on a stock exchange
By having at least 1 lakh retail investors
questions.explanation: The deck says funds can alternatively qualify by appointing experienced fund managers with a proven track record in managing large portfolios.
hints: Correct: the alternative route is experienced fund managers.
A banking licence is irrelevant.
AMC listing is not an eligibility route.
Investor count is not mentioned as a route.

questions.q: How does the new asset class differ from traditional MFs in its use of derivatives?
options: It must invest at least 50% in derivatives
It may use derivatives for purposes beyond hedging
It cannot use derivatives at all
It may use derivatives only for hedging
questions.explanation: Investment flexibility includes exposure to derivatives for purposes beyond hedging, along with proposed relaxations in single-issuer and sector limits.
hints: No minimum derivatives allocation is prescribed.
Correct: derivatives beyond hedging are permitted.
Derivatives are allowed, and more flexibly.
Hedging-only is the traditional restriction it relaxes.

questions.q: What range of dividend yields have Indian REITs delivered so far, as per the deck?
questions.explanation: REITs provide regular income with dividend yields in the range of 6 to 8% p.a. so far.
hints: 2-4% is too low.
8-10% is the InvIT range.
Correct: 6-8% for REITs.
12-15% is not mentioned.

questions.q: Which sale date is a key cut-off in determining which capital gains rules apply after Budget 2024?
questions.explanation: The 'Sell date' categories are: before July 23, 2024; on or after July 23, 2024 but before April 1, 2025; and later.
hints: January 1, 2025 is not listed.
March 31, 2023 is not a sell-date cut-off in the deck.
February 1, 2024 is not listed as a cut-off.
Correct: July 23, 2024.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed in the deck as an important concept for understanding capital gains tax?
questions.explanation: The important concepts listed are indexation, holding period, grandfathering and set-off provisions.
hints: Correct: DDT is not among the listed concepts.
Set-off provisions are listed.
Indexation is listed.
Grandfathering is listed.

questions.q: BSE was recognised as IAASB under which regulation of the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013?
questions.explanation: Recognition was granted under Regulation 14 of the RA Regulations, 2014 and IA Regulations, 2013.
hints: Regulation 15 is not cited for recognition.
Regulation 19(3) is about the annual compliance audit.
Regulation 7 is not cited for recognition.
Correct: Regulation 14.

questions.q: Adverse findings of an IA's annual compliance audit, with action taken, must reach BSE no later than which date for the previous financial year?
questions.explanation: Adverse findings must be submitted within one month from the date of the audit report but not later than October 31 of each year for the previous FY.
hints: September 30 is not the outer limit.
December 31 is too late.
Correct: not later than October 31.
June 30 is too early and not the stated date.

questions.q: For a non-individual IA, the annual certificate confirming compliance with client-level segregation must be obtained from:
questions.explanation: The certificate is from an auditor for an individual IA and from its statutory auditor for a non-individual IA, within six months of FY end.
hints: BSE receives reports; it does not certify them.
Correct: the statutory auditor.
RAs are not auditors.
The compliance officer cannot certify his own firm.

questions.q: By what date were market participants, including IAs, required to register on the ODR portal?
questions.explanation: ODR key requirements: register on the ODR portal latest by September 15, 2023.
hints: Correct: September 15, 2023.
May 01, 2023 is the display-of-details effective date.
July 25, 2024 is the BSE-IAASB start date.
March 15, 2024 is the ad approval number display date.

questions.q: When applying for BSE approval of an advertisement, what is Annexure A?
options: Details of individuals appearing in the advertisement
Confirmation of compliance with the Code of Advertisement
List of clients who will receive the ad
questions.explanation: Annexure A is the confirmation of compliance with the Code of Advertisement; Annexure B applies if the ad has individuals forming part of it.
hints: That is Annexure B.
Correct: compliance confirmation.
Client lists are not submitted.
Fee payment is separate.

questions.q: Under the advertisement code, an influencer is treated as a celebrity (and so cannot be used) if they have:
options: More than 50 lakh followers across all handles
More than 1 lakh followers in total
More than 10 lakh followers/subscribers per social media handle
Any paid partnership with a brand
questions.explanation: Celebrity includes 'an influencer with more than 10 Lacs followers/subscribers (per social media handle)'.
hints: The test is per handle and the number is 10 lakh.
1 lakh is too low a threshold.
Correct: more than 10 lakh per handle.
A paid partnership alone is not the test.

questions.q: From which date must IA advertisements display the 'BSE Limited Advertisement Approval Number'?
questions.explanation: Display of BSE Limited Advertisement Approval Number at the time of publishing is effective March 15, 2024.
hints: April 1, 2025 is not relevant.
July 25, 2024 is when BSE began as IAASB.
May 26, 2023 is the date of the BASL Code of Advertisement.
Correct: March 15, 2024.

questions.q: A third party publishes an advertisement for an IA without the IA's consent. What must the IA do?
options: Ask SEBI to approve it retrospectively
Pay the BSE fee to regularise it
Disown the advertisement, inform BSE and take appropriate legal action against the entity
Ignore it, as the IA did not issue it
questions.explanation: If a third party issues an ad without the IA's consent, the IA shall disown it, inform BSE and take appropriate legal action.
hints: There is no retrospective SEBI approval.
Paying a fee does not regularise an unauthorised ad.
Correct: disown, inform BSE, take legal action.
Ignoring it is not allowed.

questions.q: Within what time must Qualified REs obtain ISO 27001 certification under CSCRF?
options: Within 1 year of issuance of CSCRF
It is optional for Qualified REs
questions.explanation: Qualified REs shall obtain ISO 27001 within 1 year of issuance of CSCRF, and submit evidence with the cyber audit report.
hints: 5 years is not the timeline.
Correct: within 1 year.
3 months is not the timeline.
It is mandatory for Qualified REs.

questions.q: When is an RE's CSCRF category decided?
options: At the beginning of the financial year, based on the previous financial year's data
Every quarter, based on current AUM
questions.explanation: The category is decided at the beginning of the FY based on previous-FY data, and remains the same throughout that FY.
hints: Correct: start of FY using previous-FY data.
Inspections do not set the category.
It is reviewed annually, not fixed forever.
It is not re-set every quarter.

questions.q: CSCRF is divided into four parts. What does Part II contain?
options: Guidelines recommending measures to comply with the standards
questions.explanation: Part I: Objectives and Standards; Part II: Guidelines; Part III: Structured formats for compliance; Part IV: Annexures and References.
hints: That is Part III.
That is Part IV.
That is Part I.
Correct: Part II is Guidelines (a few are mandatory).

questions.q: For REs where an IT Committee is mandatory, what is the composition requirement mentioned in CSCRF?
options: It must have a majority of BSE nominees
It must be chaired by a SEBI nominee
It must include the statutory auditor
It must include at least one external independent technology expert
questions.explanation: For Mid-size and Qualified REs, the IT Committee is mandatory and must include at least one external independent technology expert.
hints: BSE nominees are not required.
No SEBI nominee is required.
The statutory auditor is not a required member.
Correct: at least one external independent technology expert.

questions.q: In a body corporate registered as an IA, who bears primary responsibility for maintaining appropriate standards of conduct?
questions.explanation: Responsibility of senior management: the senior management of a body corporate IA shall bear primary responsibility for standards of conduct and proper procedures.
hints: The auditor checks compliance but is not primarily responsible.
Clients are not responsible for the IA's conduct.
Correct: senior management.
BSE supervises but the IA's management is primarily responsible.

questions.q: Under the Code of Conduct in Schedule III of the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008, an intermediary shall not:
options: Increase any fees or charges for services rendered without proper notice
Inform SEBI of legal proceedings against it
questions.explanation: The intermediary code states it shall not increase any fees or charges for the services rendered without a proper notice.
hints: Prompt disbursal is required, not prohibited.
Correct: no fee increase without proper notice.
Informing SEBI of proceedings is required.
Backups are required.

questions.q: A SEBI order cited in the training penalised a non-individual IA for its name. What was the requirement?
options: A non-individual IA must include the words 'investment adviser' in its name
The name must include the BSE enlistment number
The name must not exceed 20 characters
questions.explanation: Case 7: the Investment Adviser, not being an individual, shall include the words 'investment adviser' in its name.
hints: Correct: 'investment adviser' must be in the name.
The enlistment number is a disclosure, not part of the name.
No length limit is cited.
Using 'SEBI registered' in the name is not the requirement.

questions.q: In one SEBI order, an IA did not hold a valid NISM X-A certification for almost how long?
questions.explanation: Case 2: the Noticee did not have a valid NISM X-A certification for almost 16 months, violating the IA Regulations.
hints: 30 days is not the period cited.
6 months is not the period cited.
3 years is not the period cited.
Correct: about 16 months.

questions.q: A client increases his equity allocation only because markets rose sharply in the last three months. Which bias is this?
questions.explanation: Recency bias is making decisions based on recent results, which can lead to incorrect conclusions; 'yesterday's truth is not tomorrow's'.
hints: Ownership bias is overvaluing what you own.
Winner's curse is overpaying to win a bid.
Correct: overweighting recent performance.
Ambiguity aversion is avoiding unknown probabilities.

questions.q: The Ellsberg paradox (choosing between a bag with 50 red/50 blue balls and a bag of unknown mix) illustrates:
questions.explanation: More people chose the bag with known 50% odds; this tendency to prefer known risks over unknown risks is ambiguity aversion.
hints: Herding is following the crowd.
Correct: ambiguity aversion.
Anchoring is relying on first information.
Confirmation bias is seeking confirming information.

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical basis for tactical/dynamic deviation from the strategic asset allocation?
questions.explanation: Tactical/dynamic allocation deviates from SAA based on opportunities, momentum, valuation changes and the fund manager's views.
hints: Correct: valuation and momentum are cited triggers.
Folio count is irrelevant.
Fee structure is irrelevant.
Date of birth is not a tactical trigger.

questions.q: The 'four truths' of asset allocation quoted in the module come from:
options: Charles D. Ellis's foreword to Roger C. Gibson's 'Asset Allocation: Balancing Financial Risk'
questions.explanation: The slides attribute the four truths to Charles D. Ellis's foreword to the 4th edition of Roger C. Gibson's Asset Allocation: Balancing Financial Risk.
hints: SEBI circulars are not the source.
Correct: Ellis's foreword to Gibson's book.
Buffett is quoted in the behavioural module, not for the four truths.
Keynes is quoted for herding, not asset allocation.
